title: The First $100K Is the Hardest: Here's the Plan
description:
Charlie Munger said the first $100,000 is the hardest. Almost nobody explains exactly how to get there from zero. In this video I break the journey into 6 stages and look at it from three angles: the numbers (how long it takes at $250, $500 or $1,000 a month), the mental trap at each stage, and a step-by-step playbook for every stage from $0 to $100K.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:28 How we got the numbers
1:55 Angle 1: The Numbers
5:29 The six stages
6:40 Angle 2: The Psychology
10:23 A quick favor
10:35 Angle 3: The Playbook
11:02 Stage 1: $0 to $1,000
12:01 Stage 2: $1,000 to $10,000
13:13 Stage 3: $10,000 to $25,000
14:15 Stage 4: $25,000 to $50,000
15:16 Stage 5: $50,000 to $75,000
16:21 Stage 6: $75,000 to $100,000
17:16 Where to keep the money at each stage
18:39 Five ways to get there faster
19:23 Finding $500 a month
20:29 The same plan at three incomes
21:24 Mistakes that cost years
22:11 Your one page tracker
23:10 Irregular income
24:09 Doing it as a couple
24:57 What about inflation?
25:36 Three paths to $100,000
27:06 What it feels like to get there
28:26 Questions people ask
31:37 Recap
32:24 What to do next

Sources:
- Charlie Munger: the first $100,000 is the hardest (widely quoted)
- Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances 2022 (median net worth under 35: $39,040; 35-44: $135,300)
- IRS, retirement plan, IRA and HSA rules and catch-up contributions (check current limits)
- Timeline and growth figures: stated illustrative math at a 7% average yearly return, compounded monthly

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video52.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
